Verso folio 442 containing recipes for a memory-preserving water, a sobriety water for drunkenness, a water for head rheums, a water to restore lost memory, a water for epilepsy ('das hin falt'), a natural-history entry with an illustration of Tutia Alexandrina, and a list of the four great and four small cooling seeds.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Tutia Alexandrina** (`#xywh=0,0,6078,6853`): Hand-drawn, washed illustration in grey and olive-green watercolor depicting a lumpy, layered mineral crust or nodule of Tutia Alexandrina (tutty / zinc oxide), positioned next to the rubricated heading 'Tutia Alexandrina' in the right column.

Recto leaf (p. 443, pencil fol. 199) containing recipes for herbal waters treating spleen and liver obstructions, jaundice, and internal/external heat, alongside a section with an illustration of two facing hands on how a physician should prepare his hands before administering pills, and a water for burned hands.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

Recto leaf (p. 445, pencil fol. 200) featuring illustrations of alchemical vessels and a smoking pipe alongside instructions for preparing Lutum Sapientiae for sealing flasks and retorts, definitions of natural and artificial days, an herbal smoking tobacco recipe, remedies for kidney gravel and stone, and a conserve for epilepsy.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Alchemical retort and flask** (`#xywh=0,0,5770,6853`): Two watercolor/ink drawings at the top of the left column above the Lutum Sapientiae heading: on the left, a brown-tinted round retort with a blue-tinted curved neck resting on a rectangular base; on the right, a round-bottomed glass flask with a long hatched neck resting on a rectangular stand; a cross '+' is drawn between them.

**Smoking pipe** (`#xywh=0,0,5770,6853`): Drawing of a long-stemmed smoking pipe (tobacco pipe) in the lower-middle left column, just above the rubricated heading for herbal smoking tobacco.

Page 447 (recto) prescribes a multi-part regimen for epilepsy and vertigo (pills, powder, decoction, amulet sachet, and bloodletting), followed by a colored anatomical drawing of an amputated human leg and a treatise on treating cold gangrene.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Amputated human leg and foot** (`#xywh=0,0,5753,6853`): Colored anatomical watercolor/ink illustration at the top of the right column depicting a severed human lower leg and foot lying on mossy green-brown ground atop a rectangular cream-colored plinth, accompanying the section on cold gangrene (Vom khalten brandt).

Folio 202r (p. 449) presents a collection of Early New High German and Latin alchemical-medical recipes, including sublimated precipitate, catarrh fumigation, turpentine pills, emetic tartar, and remedies for fistulas and nasal catarrh. The right column features a watercolor and ink illustration of a smoking censer/brazier beside a cylindrical box.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Fumigation brazier and box** (`#xywh=0,0,5753,6853`): Ink and watercolor drawing on a wooden table or shelf showing a handled metal censer/brazier on a pedestal filled with glowing red coals and rising gray smoke, next to a closed cylindrical wooden or metal box.

Folio 202v (p. 450) contains recipes for head catarrh fumigations, a medicated nasal plug (accompanied by a small watercolor drawing), epilepsy powder, gangrene treatment, quartan fever powders, a heart restorative, and an antidote for venomous animal bites.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Nasal suppository / rolled medicated plug** (`#xywh=0,0,6071,6853`): Watercolor and ink drawing of a cylindrical brown rolled plug or suppository (Zapffel) lying horizontally on a pale yellow-green surface next to the rubricated heading 'Zapffel in die Nasen'.

Folio 203r (p. 451) records recipes for hound's-tongue pills for catarrh and dropsy, a healing water for chronic sores, instructions on coloring mercury water, preventatives and diagnostic tests for epilepsy, a gout plaster, and an emollient for abscesses.

Early New High German apothecary recipes continuing the purging quince syrup, followed by stomach morsels, specialized pills (for nasal polyps, loss of taste, catarrh, throat ulcers, and bile), a precious balsam for uterine pain, three remedies for dropsy, and a fever emetic.

Page 455 (recto) presents pharmaceutical recipes and regimens for internal digestive cleansing, breast cancer (Brust Krebs), open cancerous ulcers (offner Krebs), and hidden cancer, accompanied by a hand-colored illustration of a red crayfish/crab symbolizing cancer, as well as recipes for carnation conserve and golden water for fluxes.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Crayfish / Crab Illustration (Cancer Symbol)** (`#xywh=0,0,5809,6853`): Hand-colored drawing in red and brown wash depicting a crayfish or crab centered below the rubricated heading 'Ein bad Miedl in Brust Krebs.', serving as a visual emblem for cancer (Krebs).

Page 457 (recto) begins a treatise on hemorrhoids (Gülden Ader) and anal warts/condylomata (Feigwartzen), explaining how to diagnose their humoral composition (bile, phlegm, melancholy) and how to apply blood-sucking leeches (Blutegel) to relieve them, illustrated by a large colored scene of a seated bearded man leaning over a basin on a stool.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Seated Man at a Low Table with Basin** (`#xywh=0,0,5769,6853`): Large hand-colored illustration in the upper-left column depicting a bearded man in a red robe seated on a wooden bench, leaning forward with his hands over a shallow red-rimmed basin resting on a four-legged wooden stool; a stoneware jug and a small hand-broom sit beside the bench on a green ground.

Instructions for applying leeches to hemorrhoidal veins, including a rubricated warning on removing a leech that enters the body using salted water and directions for using a perforated stool with a candle for continuous heat. Continues with a section on hemorrhoidal pain ('Volgt Weider Von den Schmerzen der hemoroides'), prescribing gentle clysters, laxatives (cassia, tamarinds), bloodletting, Unguentum Linariae, and a compound ointment with poplar buds, opium, and balsam.

Recipes for preparing Unguentum Linariae and other pain-relieving ointments for blind hemorrhoids (containing litharge, henbane oil, ceruse, tutia, saffron, opium, and rose/violet oils). Begins a new major section on excessive hemorrhoidal bleeding ('Von dem Excess Vnd überfluß der Gulden Ader'), detailing bloodletting from the liver vein or salvatella, cupping, and astringent/cooling syrups and boluses.

Continues astringent and styptic recipes for stopping excessive hemorrhoidal bleeding (containing Armenian bole, terra sigillata, red coral, hematite, mumia, comfrey, camphor, dragon's blood, and crocus martis), accompanied by a coloured illustration of a reclining patient in a red-striped garment. Begins a new section on anal ulcers and fistulas ('Von den Geschwer Vnd fistl in Ano'), describing their causes, internal channels, and examination with a speculum ani.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Reclining patient figure (Right Column, middle)** (`#xywh=0,0,6013,6853`): Coloured ink and wash illustration framed in a ruled rectangle, depicting a figure draped in a red-and-white striped garment reclining on green ground with knees raised and bent, illustrating the posture for applying topical remedies or examining anal ulcers/fistulas.

Remedies for anal ulcers (diet, herbal decoction, ointments/salves, and plasters) transitioning to the exploration and surgical treatment of anal fistulas, illustrated with four surgical instruments (two curved grooved directors, a bulbous probe, and a curved bistoury).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Surgical instruments for exploring and cutting fistulas (two curved grooved directors/syringotomes, a bulbous probe, and a curved bistoury)** (`#xywh=0,0,5783,6853`): Pen-and-ink wash drawing of four surgical instruments arranged vertically in the right column: on the left, two curved, tapered grooved directors or fistula knives (syringotomes) shaded in brown wash; in the center, a slender dark-shaded probe with a bulbous, segmented handle at the bottom; on the right, a curved bistoury or scalpel with a dark, ornate handle and a curved single-edged blade.

Discussion of fontanels (issues / cauteria) as alternatives to fistula surgery, with a watercolor illustration of a seated male figure marked with red spots for fontanel placement sites, followed by methods of creating fontanels (cutting, burning, corrosive), anatomical placement list, and recipes for soothing lead-mercury plates and cantharides pills.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Anatomical diagram showing fontanel (issue) placement sites on the human body** (`#xywh=0,0,5801,6853`): Pen-and-ink and watercolor drawing of a seated nude male figure seen from behind and in three-quarter profile, with his left arm raised and legs bent, resting on a rectangular wooden-style plinth. Small red circular spots mark specific anatomical sites for fontanels (issues) on the head, neck, upper arm, forearm, thigh, knee, and lower leg.

Treatise on kidney/bladder stones, sand, and gravel ('Von Stain sandt Vnd Jrieß'), featuring an illustration of an apothecary at a worktable with flasks, followed by recipes for woodlice powder, turpentine syrup, stone powders, pills, clysters, and draughts.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Von Stain sandt Vnd Jrieß** (`#xywh=0,0,5773,6853`): Hand-colored ink and watercolor illustration in the upper-left corner of the page depicting a bearded apothecary or physician with brown hair, dressed in a red doublet/coat with white cuffs, yellow-ochre breeches, and red stockings, leaning over a wooden table with glass alchemical flasks and vials (including a large round-bottomed flask filled with green liquid). Below the figure is a small landscape vignette with green grass, a brown bush/tree, and grey rocky ground.

Continuation of remedies for stone, sand, and gravel, including laxative draughts and boluses, Jadanius's pills, herbal drinks, herbal baths, sand pills, a precious water distilled with snails, and ointments for urinary obstruction and colic.

Remedies for kidney/bladder gravel and stones (including ivy, frog/elder, Venetian turpentine with five distilled waters, pigeon dung, and a multi-herb gravel bath), followed by a powder for gravel and phlegm, further recipes (woodlice, sal ammoniac, pigeon dung, garlic/onion trituration), an illustration of a urine flask/jug and chamber pot, and a section on obstructed urine (strangury/dysuria).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Urine jug/flask and handled chamber pot on a wooden table** (`#xywh=0,0,5759,6853`): Centered in the right column above 'Den Verstopfften Vrin zu dreib'. On the left is a tapering blue-grey glass or ceramic pitcher/flask with a flared rim and bulbous base half-filled with golden-amber liquid, resting on a coiled yellow straw ring. On the right is a wide, low dark grey/black earthenware or pewter chamber pot with a single loop handle on the right side. Both vessels sit on a brown wooden table or shelf.

Continuation of diuretic remedies, a julep to drive urine, two herbal baths for urinary obstruction and gravel/stone pain, a lizard-based diuretic, a distilled water for gravel/stone and hernia carnosa, a strawberry-based colic/gravel remedy, an illustration of a urine matula/flask with a red urine symbol, and definitions/descriptions of dysuria, strangury, and diabetes.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Urine flask (matula) on a wooden table with red urine symbol (⊡)** (`#xywh=0,0,6013,6853`): Positioned in the middle of the right column next to the rubricated heading 'Disuria Strangúgria Hernia harn.' A cylindrical blue-grey glass flask (matula) with a flared rim, narrow neck, and bulbous base containing golden-amber liquid, resting on a coiled yellow straw ring. It sits on a brown wooden table/box with a blank white rectangular label panel on the front. To the upper right of the flask is a square with a central dot (⊡) drawn in red ink.

Continuation of the treatise on strangury and urinary obstruction: causes (swollen bladder neck, caruncles, stones, coagulated blood, ulcer matter, thick phlegm), involuntary urination from nerve paralysis vs. muscle weakness, diagnostic examination with a catheter, and external/internal treatments (oils, plasters, fumigations, baths, syrups, and stone-breaking remedies).

Remedies for urinary complaints (strangury/retention and nocturnal enuresis / inability to hold urine, marked with the square urine/bladder symbol), followed by a rubricated section on Gonorrhoea with a blank pasted rectangular label/box, describing its causes (weakness of retaining power vs. excessive expelling power, heat in the vasa spermatica), symptoms, and dietary/regimen precautions.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Blank pasted label under 'Gonorrchea'** (`#xywh=0,0,5746,6853`): A blank, cream-colored rectangular paper slip framed in red ink, positioned directly beneath the rubricated heading 'Gonorrchea' in the upper-middle left of the right column, with a small ink dot near the center.

Section on ulcers of the genitals/penis ('Von Geschwer des ♀'), detailing diet, purgation, warm cow's milk baths, soothing mucilage injections, and turpentine pills; followed in the right column by a watercolor anatomical diagram of the urinary bladder and urethra and a section distinguishing between bladder stones and urethral caruncles ('Von Undter schidt Der Griesen Zwischen dem Stain Und Carnuncula') using a bougie/catheter.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Anatomical diagram of the urinary bladder and urethra** (`#xywh=0,0,5772,6853`): A framed watercolor illustration in the middle of the right column depicting a rounded, orange-reddish urinary bladder with two sinuous/coiled ureters entering at the upper left and upper right, and a curved, tapering bladder neck/urethra descending downward to the right. Directly beneath the illustration is a blank rectangular label box framed in red ink.

Remedies for urinary obstruction, urethral flesh/strictures using bougies (candela), and the beginning of a section on bladder ulcers ('Von Geschwer der Blasen') accompanied by a framed anatomical illustration of the urinary bladder.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Anatomical illustration of the urinary bladder** (`#xywh=0,0,6019,6853`): A hand-drawn anatomical illustration in red-brown ink and wash, framed in a square box in the upper-left portion of the right column beside the rubricated heading 'Von Geschwer der Blasen'. It depicts the urinary bladder as an ovoid sac with two sinuous ureters entering from the upper left and upper right sides, and a curved urethra extending downward and curving to the right.

Further remedies and diagnostic distinctions between kidney, ureter, and bladder ulcers, followed by a section on bladder ulcers following gonorrhea and fleshy growths (carnositides) in the urinary canal, accompanied by a small anatomical diagram.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Anatomical diagram of a urethral caruncle / bladder neck obstruction** (`#xywh=0,0,6073,6853`): A small hand-drawn anatomical illustration in brown and reddish-brown ink and wash, positioned in the right column just above the rubricated heading 'Weilen aber nach denen Geschweren'. It shows an ovoid bladder-like sac on the right tapering into a narrow horizontal canal/tube extending to the left, illustrating a fleshy growth (carnositides) or obstruction in the urinary canal.

Continuation of recipes for urethral/inguinal ulcers and carnosities (including a collyrium and Emplastrum de ranis cum mercurio Vigonis), followed by a new rubricated section on hot swellings and apostemes of the testicles and scrotum, detailing humoral causes and systemic purging/bloodletting cures.

A new treatise on ruptures (hernias) of the body, illustrated with a hand-coloured figure of a man wearing a hernia truss, classifying five types of hernias and true vs. incomplete ruptures, followed by four precious rupture plasters.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Anatomical figure of a standing man wearing a hernia truss** (`#xywh=0,0,5793,6853`): Hand-coloured pen-and-ink wash illustration in the upper-left area of the page depicting a standing, beardless man with shoulder-length curly brown hair, naked except for a red and yellow sash/truss tied around his waist and groin (hernia bandage/suspensory). His right hand rests on his chest while his left hand holds out the long trailing red-and-yellow band of the truss. He stands on a small patch of brownish-green ground.

Two-column page continuing the discussion of Hernia Carnosa (with Emplastrum de ranis cum mercurio of Giovanni da Vigo), followed by Hernia Varicosa sanguinosa (varicocele), a section on groin swellings (Von den Triesten in Reichen), and concluding remedies for ruptures and Hernia aquosa (hydrocele), accompanied by a small oval red-ink diagram.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Unlabeled oval red-ink anatomical/hernia diagram** (`#xywh=0,0,6013,6853`): Small shaded oval/pear-shaped drawing in reddish-brown ink positioned to the left of the rubricated heading 'Volgen noch slüß mitl Vor die brüch' in the lower right column, depicting a swelling or scrotal/hernial sac.

Treatise on encysted tumors and swellings (Atheroma, Steatoma, Meliceris, Ganglion, Struma/Scrofula), including plaster recipes, an anatomical/surgical illustration of a man with multiple tumors, and surgical excision instructions.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**(Unlabeled anatomical/surgical illustration showing a man with tumors)** (`#xywh=0,0,6044,6853`): A colored pen-and-ink and watercolor illustration in the upper half of the right column. It depicts a nude male figure from the waist up, turned in three-quarter view to the left, with short blond hair. In his raised right hand he holds a tall dark blue-grey cylindrical cup or vessel. Several circular reddish-brown swellings or encysted tumors (illustrating atheroma, steatoma, meliceris, etc.) are drawn on his left cheek, the side of his neck, his left shoulder, a large one on his right chest/breast, and one on his right elbow.

Continuation of surgical excision and caustic treatment of encysted tumors, warning against operating on growths near the spine, followed by an illustration of a woman with a shoulder tumor and recipes for softening hard boils and apostemes.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**(Unlabeled anatomical/surgical illustration showing a woman with a shoulder tumor)** (`#xywh=0,0,5776,6853`): A colored pen-and-ink and watercolor illustration in the upper portion of the right column. It depicts a nude female figure from the chest up, facing forward with her head slightly turned to the left and her blonde hair swept back. Her right arm is raised with her hand open beside her face. On her left shoulder, a prominent raised circular reddish-brown swelling or tumor is depicted.

Illustrated treatise and recipes on treating burns and scalds caused by water, oil, gunpowder, or wax, including cooling salves, lime-water washes, and eye-protecting ointments.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Kitchen/laboratory scene illustrating scalding and burns** (`#xywh=0,0,5784,6853`): Coloured ink-and-wash illustration in the upper-left column depicting a woman in a blue bodice, white apron, and red skirt standing in a doorway with her right hand raised in alarm, looking toward a brick hearth where a large cauldron hangs over a blazing fire from a chain and wooden beam, with pots, a ladle, and spilled liquid on the hearth and jars and pans on a shelf above.

Discourse on sympathetic healing and transplantation, recounting conversations with a Jesuit (Father Bernardin) and a Bishop defending sympathetic powder as a natural effect rather than a diabolical pact, followed by a definition of sympathetic healing using copper vitriol.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

Continuation of sympathetic and magnetic cures involving blood, urine, milk, and herbs (Persicaria), followed by a rubricated section on the transplantation of diseases into animal or vegetable subjects (e.g., into an egg, an anthill, a dog, or an elder bush, and transplantation of gout/podagra into a wormwood bush citing Timaeus), and a theoretical discussion of the volatile spiritus vitalis.

Continuation of the discourse on the spiritus vitalis and Mumia (nails, hair, sweat, urine, blood), followed by a first-person account of curing a preacher's severe hand pain in Graz using sympathetic powder on a bloodied cloth, and a rubricated section detailing strict hygienic and ritual rules for handling the bloodied cloths (avoiding menstrual contamination, dust, cold, garlic, onions, and pork).

Illustrated recipes for 'Cichori Fluët' (a blood-purifying chicory and germander extract) and 'Puluis Simpateticus' (sympathetic powder), including two colored illustrations (botanical plants and an emblematic solar/Leo scene) and detailed instructions for preparing the powder during August when the Sun is in Leo, plus its application to stop severe bleeding.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Cichori Fluët. Ein herliche Reinigung des geblüets.** (`#xywh=0,0,5758,6853`): Colored botanical illustration in the upper-left corner of the left column depicting two plants growing from a grassy hillock: a smaller plant with blue flowers (chicory) on the left and a taller woody shrub or tree with red blossoms/leaves on the right.

**Puluis Simpateticus, Wie es gemacht Und Gebraucht Wirdt.** (`#xywh=0,0,5758,6853`): Colored emblematic scene spanning the left column, framed by blue horizontal borders. In the sky, a golden sun shines yellow rays diagonally down onto a banded cylindrical vessel resting on a stone pedestal on the left, while a golden lion (Leo) leaps among clouds at upper left. Below, in a grassy landscape with distant hills, a seated figure in a green doublet and red breeches extends a thin wand or thread toward the vessel.

Sympathetic remedies using vitriol/powder (♃) and blood/urine (□) for wounds, fevers, excessive menstruation, and burns, followed by a defense of natural magic and sympathetic powder against accusations of sorcery, recounting a 1696 dinner conversation with Jesuit Father Höpel at Herberstein's estate in Laboth.

Continuation of the defense of sympathetic remedies (citing the Bishop of Lavant, Stadion, and Parisian theologians), followed by a section on the transplantation of diseases into animals and trees, illustrated with a watercolor scene of a dog eating from a tub and a man working on a tree.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Transplantation of disease into a dog and a tree** (`#xywh=0,0,5735,6853`): Colored watercolor and ink illustration in the middle of the right column. At the upper left is a yellow sun with a face and stylized blue-grey clouds. On the left, a brown dog eats from a wooden tub/bucket. On the right, a man in a yellow coat and red breeches stands before a large green deciduous tree, boring or plugging a hole in its trunk. A blue horizontal line borders the bottom of the scene.

Reflections on accepting gout as God's penance rather than transferring it to a faithful dog, followed by sympathetic tree-transplantation cures for limb atrophy and childhood hernias (passing a naked child through a split sapling at new moon), and the beginning of a new section 'Anatomia der Wundt Kreidter' with an illustration of four flowering wound-herbs.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Four flowering wound-herbs (Wundkräuter)** (`#xywh=0,0,6014,6853`): Colored watercolor and ink illustration in the middle of the right column above the rubricated heading 'Anatomia der Wundt Kreidter.' Four flowering herbs grow side by side in brown soil, each with green stems and leaves: from left to right, pale blue/white flowers, yellow flowers, red flowers, and yellow-green/amber flowers.

Continuation of the human cranium preparation; followed by rubricated recipes 'Von krebs augen' (On crabs' eyes), 'Magisterium Von kreps Augen' (Magisterium of crabs' eyes), 'Ciderani. ▽.' (Ciderani water), 'Hundt Leben Machen Nim Grosse vnd Wunnderliche Wirckhung' (accompanied by an illustration of a fluted glass flask), and 'Guldtne Milch' (Golden milk).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Fluted glass flask (right column, beside 'Hundt Leben Machen')** (`#xywh=0,0,6040,6853`): A hand-drawn and painted illustration positioned on the left side of the right column alongside the rubricated heading 'Hundt Leben Machen Nim Grosse vnd Wunnderliche Wirckhung'. It depicts a round-bottomed, vertically ribbed/fluted glass flask or phial with a narrow neck and flared lip, shaded in blue-grey wash to indicate glass transparency, resting on a tan/ochre rectangular table or stand with a cast shadow.

Alchemical and chemical recipes: continuation of a recipe with mace and cloves; silver-plating brass ('Mößing Zu VerSilbern'); cosmetic/medicinal 'Maill Khugl' with two drawn spheres; another ball recipe; making a bone/ivory ('Ein Pain Zu Machen'); a stone/bone that always gives fire ('Pain der Aderzeit feuer gibt'); distilling oil from a brick ('Oll auß einen Zieg Zu brinen'); making water from salt and sal ammoniac in a black radish ('Waßer auß ⊖ ✶ Zu machen'); making a pleasant scent in a chimney/room; and 'Vom Pain Essenz' (bone essence) for spleen, liver obstructions, and constipation.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Maill Khugl** (`#xywh=0,0,6054,6853`): Two small shaded circular drawings of round balls or spheres (possibly medicinal or cosmetic soap balls) placed in the left column directly to the left of the rubricated heading 'Maill Khugl'.

Medical treatise on joint disease and gout ('Von der Glider Sucht. Arthritis'), featuring a large colored illustration of a man on crutches and a woman offering a cup. Discusses persistent vs. wandering gout (Podagra in the feet, Chiragra in the hands), accompanying fever, loss of appetite, and the role of a sharp sour salt humor obstructing nourishment and gnawing at the periosteum and nerves.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Von der Glider Sucht. Arthritis** (`#xywh=0,0,5712,6853`): Colored pen-and-ink and watercolor illustration in the upper left column depicting a male patient suffering from gout/arthritis and a female attendant. On the left, a bearded man wearing a green-and-yellow turban-like cap and a long reddish-brown belted coat walks hunched forward on two wooden crutches, looking toward the right. On the right, a woman in a blue-and-red bodice with a plumed headdress stands behind a green upholstered high-backed chair, extending a small dark cup or goblet in her right hand toward the man. Below the illustration is the rubricated title 'Von der Glider Sucht. Arthritis'.

Continuation of the treatise on arthritis/gout: distinguishing Podagra from true arthritis; the causes of the disease ('Die Vrsach diser khranckheit sind Vnderschidlich'), including overeating/overdrinking, anger, strong wine, sharp brain fluxes, heavy lifting, and chilling; prognosis (generally not fatal and often associated with longevity, though dangerous in weak old age, potentially leading to fever, pleurisy, stroke, or palpitations); and treatment via diet, abstention from wine and sour foods, purging/evacuation, and prescribed pills followed by mineral salt and oil.

Continuation of recipes and humoral theory regarding podagra (gout) and the use of hermodactili (autumn crocus) with purgatives, followed by a rubricated secretum for arthritic/gouty patients (an infusion of bryony, hermodactili, mechoacanna, China root, agaric, rhubarb, sandalwood, myrobalans, sassafras, coriander, juniper, chicory, and tartar), a soothing limb salve, red-ink notes on blood purification, and a germander-must cure.

Recipes for external plasters, internal purgations (with mercurius dulcis, hermodactili, jalap, scammony, agaric, and extracts) for gout and joint pains, external washes, oils (oleum cerae, tobacco oil, earthworm oil), a burnt earthworm powder for wounds and dropsy, and a rubricated section on Arthritis Vaga (wandering gout).

Continuation of the treatment of Arthritis Vaga (wandering gout), covering laxatives, bloodletting and inspecting the blood, absorbent powders, a famous gout powder, crystal powder, an herbal broth drink, dietary rules (avoiding sour, salted, and heavy foods), and an external compress with spirit of earthworms, sal ammoniac, scurvy-grass, Venetian soap, opium, and saffron.

Anatomical illustration of the human spinal cord (with 30 numbered vertebrae) and branching nervous system, followed by a rubricated section on the origin and diseases of the nerves (47 nerves from brain and spinal cord, 60 from the spine, spiritus animales, apoplexy, contractures, and injuries from cold, vapors, and dryness).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**** (`#xywh=400,400,2320,1000`): Anatomical illustration in blue wash and black/brown ink occupying the upper two-thirds of the left column, depicting a standing human figure on a green-brown grassy mound above a double blue horizontal border. The central spinal column is drawn with 30 individually numbered vertebrae (1–30), from which blue branching nerves radiate outward into the head, arms, hands, torso, legs, and feet.

Continuation on nerve injuries from sharp humors and gout, followed by recipes for nerve oils, ointments, and fomentations (in cold and hot causes), and a rubricated section on nerves bruised or injured by a knife (distinguishing cut, slit, and punctured nerves).

Recipes and treatments for nerve injuries during bloodletting, inflamed nerves, severed or torn nerves, nerve wounds with frost and itching, pain in wounds, and slackened nerves (including euphorbium salve, balsam, lead/gold tincture, and Emplastrum sticticum Crolli).

Introduction to the chapter on gout (Podagra) and its remedies, featuring an illustration of a seated man with gouty feet resting on a pillow alongside a verse on patient suffering, followed by medical theory on hot and cold gout, a rubricated note on prevention, and several compound recipes including Electuario Caricostino and purgative pills.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Für dein Kranckheit ist khein Khraudt...** (`#xywh=400,400,2123,1000`): Colored ink and wash illustration of a bearded man suffering from gout (Podagra) seated in a wooden armchair. He wears a red fur-trimmed coat, a red cap with grey fur trim, and mustard-yellow boots/stockings, with both feet resting on a round white-grey cushion on the ground. He holds a long wooden staff or crutch horizontally across his lap with both hands.

Continuation of gout remedies, including herbal footbaths for strengthening weak gouty feet (illustrated with a figure soaking feet in a wooden tub), an earthworm oil secretum, an apothecary bottle illustration with instructions for applying the oil, and a 'miraculous remedy' using cat fat and vinegar.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Ein khöstliches Badt für die Podagraische schwache füeß.** (`#xywh=400,400,2323,1000`): Colored ink and wash illustration in the lower left column depicting a person's bare lower legs and feet (from the thighs/knees down) soaking in a round, hooped wooden tub filled with water.

**Die Artzeney wird also gebraucht.** (`#xywh=400,400,2323,1000`): Colored ink and wash illustration in the upper-middle right column depicting a rectangular blue-grey apothecary glass bottle with a narrow neck and flared lip, resting on a yellow-brown circular base.

Page 527 (fol. 233) containing a medicinal wine and several purgative powders for gout, followed by the famous recipe for Queen Elizabeth of Hungary's Water (Aqua Reginae Hungariae), illustrated with a golden royal crown and a small red apothecary jar.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Volgen Andere der gleichen, Khöstliche Pulluer für die Podagraische** (`#xywh=400,400,2156,1000`): Small colored illustration on the left margin/border of the left column depicting a small red cylindrical apothecary jar or capsule with a dark grey/blue rim at top and bottom.

**Der Khünigin Elisabeth in Ungern Von Gott geoffen bahrtes ▽ für das Podagra** (`#xywh=400,400,2156,1000`): Colored ink and wash illustration in the middle of the right column depicting a golden royal crown with a red velvet cap/lining and jeweled/ornamented rim, resting on a yellow-brown base.

Early New High German medical recipes for purgatives (using scammony, turpeth, mechoacana, hermodactyl, black hellebore, and diaphoretic antimony), pain-relieving poultices (woman's milk, rose water, egg yolk, cow's milk), cleansing powders, and a detailed herbal bath and wine infusion regimen.

Continuation of the wine regimen, a precious water for podagra in the feet, and a major illustrated treatise 'Von dem Schiatica' (Of Sciatica) describing its humoral pathology, three diagnostic signs, sudorific treatments (sassafras, lignum sanctum, china root, sarsaparilla), and a pitch-plaster cure.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Illustration of a man suffering from sciatica (Von dem Schiatica)** (`#xywh=400,400,2153,1000`): A hand-colored ink and watercolor illustration positioned on the left side of the left column next to the heading 'Von dem Schiatica'. It depicts a bearded man in profile facing left, hunched forward in pain and leaning heavily on a wooden walking stick or crutch held in his right hand. He wears a yellow-ochre doublet/jacket with rolled sleeves, dark brown breeches, tan stockings, and brown shoes, standing on a patch of green grass.

Clysters, plasters, cerates, and ointments for sciatica, podagra, and limb pains, including recipes with cowslip, betony, bryony root, dwarf elder juice, pine resin, ship's pitch, galbanum, wormwood juice, ox gall, rectified mercury, and green pomegranates.

Recipes for sciatica (including internal infusions, an artificial bath, and electuaries/ointments), a wound-healing plaster, a secretum for sciatica and gout, a remedy for swollen feet from podagra (illustrated with a watercolor of a foot in a wooden tub), and an aqua recipe.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Foot in a wooden tub (podagra footbath)** (`#xywh=400,400,2155,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the lower right column beside the rubricated heading 'Ein Köstliches Mitel für Groß Geschwollne füeß Von Podagra'. It depicts a bare lower leg and foot (flesh-toned) immersed in blue-tinted water inside a brown hooped wooden tub or bucket resting on a yellowish-brown round base.

Treatise on erysipelas ('Von der Schön' / St. Anthony's fire), illustrated with a watercolor of a seated man with inflamed, swollen lower legs, followed by internal and external remedies, fumigant powders, and poultices ('Umb Schlag').

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Seated man with erysipelas ('Die Schön') on his lower legs** (`#xywh=400,400,2306,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the upper left column beside the rubricated heading 'Von der Schön'. It depicts a seated man in profile facing right, wearing a white/pinkish shirt and yellowish-brown breeches, sitting on a grey stone block. His exposed lower legs and feet are markedly swollen, inflamed, and bright reddish-orange, illustrating erysipelas.

Continuation of poultices, ointments, and powders for erysipelas ('Ein Sälbel Zur Schön Und Hitzigen Schäden', 'Volgentes Pulvier Ist ein fertiges Schatz für die Schön'), followed by a treatise on knee swellings ('Von Khine Schwaam') illustrated with a watercolor of a swollen knee, and remedies for mixed apostemes.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Swollen knee ('Khine Schwaam')** (`#xywh=400,400,2174,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the lower left column beside the rubricated heading 'Von Khine Schwaam.' and the pencil foliation '236'. It depicts a bare bent leg (flesh-toned) resting on a patch of pale green/yellowish ground, showing a prominent, inflamed, reddish-brown swelling on the knee joint.

Recipes for cold swellings of the knees (plasters and cataplasms to resolve, dry, and soften hard swellings), followed by surgical instructions for incising knee-water ('Wie die Khnie Wasser am Best Geschniden Werd'), accompanied by an illustration of a seated man with a swollen knee.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**** (`#xywh=400,400,2306,1000`): Color wash illustration in the lower-left quadrant showing a man in a pinkish-red tunic seated on a rectangular stone block, facing right in three-quarter profile with hands clasped over his chest and bare legs/feet resting on a dark greenish-brown sloped ground. His forward (right) knee appears slightly swollen. Framed by a thin red-ink border on top and bottom, a thick red-ink vertical band separating it from the right-hand text column, and an empty rectangular label box below.

Continuation of post-incision wound care for knee-water, followed by remedies for joint-water ('glid Wasser') and a section on swollen feet ('Volgt Weider Von den geschwollnen fiesen') featuring vapor-bath and footbath recipes with two illustrations.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**** (`#xywh=400,400,2134,1000`): Color wash illustration in the upper-middle of the right column showing a white cloth draped over a shallow three-legged pan or brazier filled with glowing red coals/embers, resting on a yellow-ochre surface, illustrating a vapor/fumigation treatment for swollen feet.

Footbath recipes for gouty and swollen feet, a clinical discussion distinguishing hot vs. cold humors in foot swellings ('Von Underschidt der geschwulst an fiesen'), a cataplasm and plaster recipe, and a section on watery swellings ('Tumor aquosus. Wäßerige geschwulst').

Surgical and medical recipes for flatulent tumors (Tumor flatulentus) from winds and fluxes, and for cold, phlegmatic tumors on the feet, knees, and arms, including herbal poultice bags, a watercolor illustration of a bent leg, cataplasms, ointments (Unguentum Agrippa), cherry-gum plasters, and internal/external decoctions.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Cold tumor on the leg and foot (in 'Von denen khalten Tumoren an denen fießen vnd armen')** (`#xywh=400,400,2181,1000`): Colored ink and watercolor illustration placed in the lower-middle portion of the left column, showing a bare human right leg bent at the knee, resting on a green grassy mound. The leg faces left, illustrating cold, phlegmatic swelling around the knee, calf, and foot.

Continuation of poultices and plasters for cold swellings (including Emplastrum de Cumino, Emplastrum de Baccis Lauri, and cataplasms with mercury and bryony), followed by a section on old ulcers and sores on the feet ('Von alle Schäden an fießen'), accompanied by an illustration of a seated man with ulcerated legs.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Seated man with ulcerated legs (above 'Von alle Schäden an fießen')** (`#xywh=400,400,2318,1000`): Colored ink and watercolor illustration at the top of the right column depicting a man seated on a wooden chest/bench inside a room with a paned window and a small wooden table. He wears a pink/reddish tunic and yellow breeches, bending forward to hold and examine his bare swollen lower leg and foot, which display red sores/ulcers on the shin, ankle, and top of the foot.

Continuation of remedies for old, inflamed, and ulcerated foot sores, including cooling waters, Emplastrum Griseum, a wound drink ('Volgentes Wundt Tranckh', numbered 239 in red ink), a healing bath for stubborn old sores, 'Bälbel St. Jax' ointment, a lead-and-calamine plaster, a cooling liniment, an unguent, and 'Bälbel So fleiß Macht'.

Surgical recipes and instructions for testing and dulcifying mercury precipitate, preparing lead-mercury ointments and wound salves, an incarnative wound powder, a note on internal purgation and antimony-sarsaparilla decoction for shinbone ulcers, and a cleansing powder made with orpiment.

Recipes for an incarnative ointment and astringent powder for open sores, accompanied by a watercolor illustration of ulcerated and bandaged lower legs, followed by red-ink rubricated clinical observations on hot phlegmonous leg ulcers, a cataplasm, litharge ointment, oak-ash lye wound water, and a red-ink-headed powder and plaster recipe.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Lower-leg ulceration and bandaging on a seated patient** (`#xywh=400,400,2152,1000`): Rectangular watercolor and ink illustration in the left column on a pale ochre ground showing the bare lower legs and feet of a seated figure wearing red breeches tucked above the knees. The right leg (viewer's left) displays scattered red pustules and small open sores on the shin and calf; the left leg (viewer's right) is wrapped around the mid-calf with a dark grey-blue cloth bandage, with red sores visible above and below the bandage.

Recipes for a birthwort-tea-amalgam wound water, a calamine-litharge-lapis medicamentosus plaster, a watercolor illustration of an ulcerated lower leg resting on a wooden footstool, a red-ink heading on putrid and callous ulcers, and recipes for aqua phagedaenica and herbal-antimonial wound washes and powders.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Ulcerated lower leg resting on a wooden footstool** (`#xywh=400,400,2320,1000`): Rectangular watercolor and ink illustration in the left column on a pale ochre ground depicting a bare lower leg from above the knee to the foot, resting horizontally with the heel supported on a small four-legged wooden stool and the thigh resting on a round wooden block. Multiple dark red and brownish ulcerative lesions are visible along the shin, ankle, and upper foot.

Surgical recipes and treatise on old, malignant leg ulcers and sores ('Von Alten üblen Schäden Und geschweer an Painen'), including plasters, cataplasms, fomentations, and a section on cancerous/phagedenic ulcers ('Die Geschweer Von einer Vmb sich fressentem...'). Features a watercolor illustration of a leg with red sores resting on a wooden block.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**** (`#xywh=400,400,2164,1000`): Rectangular framed watercolor illustration in the middle of the left column depicting a bare human lower leg and foot resting the heel on a cylindrical wooden block on a greenish-yellow ground, with multiple reddish-brown circular lesions and ulcers along the shin and calf.

Continuation of recipes for cancerous/phagedenic ulcers and superfluous flesh, followed by a treatise and remedies for frostbitten feet and hands ('Erfrore Fieß', 'Für das beißen Und schmertz der Füeß Und hend', 'Wan man Sich Erfrert'). Features a watercolor illustration of a bandaged lower leg resting on a wooden block.

Conclusion of the frostbite section, followed by short recipes for foot ailments ('Vor das gefranß der Füeß', 'Vor mietigkeit der Füeß', 'Vor die aufgesprungne Fersen') and the beginning of a treatise on cramps and convulsions ('Khram. Spamus. Conuulsion'). Features a watercolor illustration of a nude man suffering a convulsion on a bed.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**242** (`#xywh=400,400,2166,1000`): Rectangular watercolor illustration at the bottom of the left column depicting a nude man lying on a yellow-ochre bed with a white bolster/pillow, his limbs and torso tensed in a convulsive spasm, with a dark backdrop and a brownish-green landscape to the right; numbered '242' in faint red-brown ink at the upper left of the frame.

Continuation of prognostic signs for cramps/spasms (when fatal after wounds, purging, dysentery, hellebore, or fevers), followed by a section on curing the cramp condition ('Chur über disen Chram Zuestands') with internal decoctions, purging pills, liniments/ointments, a home mineral-style bath ('Bad ex ▽.'), aromatic waters, and powders for cramps from cold, phlegm, or evacuation.

Left column continues cramp regimen (keeping the patient warm and in the dark), outlines a digestive and laxative cure, uterine extension/suffocation cramps, and clyster recipes. Right column features a framed watercolor illustration of a bedridden patient beneath 'Stirbt so stirbt der Patient —', followed by a new section 'Contractura.' discussing bilious and tartaric causes of limb contracture and initial purgative/antimony tincture treatment.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Contractura.** (`#xywh=400,400,2142,1000`): Framed rectangular watercolor and ink illustration at the top of the right column, beneath the line 'Stirbt so stirbt der Patient —' and above the large rubricated heading 'Contractura.'. It depicts a patient wearing a striped headscarf/nightcap, propped up on white pillows in a wooden bed with a carved headboard and footboard. The patient's upper torso is bare and the lower body is covered by a green/teal blanket over white bedsheets.

Full-width single-column page continuing the treatment of contracture ('Contractura'). Includes a gentle purgative infusion, an ordinary medicinal drink ('Volgentes Trankh Soll hir ordinarij geben Werden.'), and a series of therapeutic baths and herbal/metallic washes for contracted, lame, and painful limbs ('Folgen die Bäder...', 'Ein Anders. für Contracte glider...', 'Ein Anders für Lame Glider.', 'Ein Bad in großen glider schmerzen', 'Ein Bad die Glider zu stärkhen'), concluding with the start of 'Köstliches Wasser in der Contractur'.

Continuation of a guaiacum and rhubarb electuary/decoction recipe with an ointment for evening application; followed by a section on Tremor (trembling of the hands or limbs), its causes, prognosis, pills for trembling (castoreum, asafoetida, colocynth, centaury), an electuary (Volgente Lattwerung) with myrobalans and spices, remedies for trembling caused by mercury/quicksilver or poisonous ores (theriac, masterwort, angelica, sweating and herbal baths), and the start of a proven ointment and bath for lame limbs.

Continuation of the 18-day bath, ointment (Die Salben Mach also), and medicinal wine drink (Volgentes Tranck Solle der Krancke Trincken) for lame limbs; followed by a major section on Phlegmon or inflammation of a limb (Von der phlegmone oder Entzündung eines Glidts), its anatomical nomenclature (ophthalmia, angina, pleuritis, erysipelas, panaritium, furunculus, anthrax, ranula, buboes, parotis), causes involving volatile salt, bloodletting, and purgatives (resin of jalap).

Continuation of internal and external remedies for phlegmon/inflammation (including antimony, sal ammoniac, laudanum, spirit of hartshorn, spermaceti, diaphoretic antimony, pike's jawbone, unicorn horn, and volatile-salt herbs), followed by external resolvents vs. repellents, and a new section on cold watery swellings or oedema (Von Kalten Wäserigen Geschwulsten. oedema), prescribing diet, guaiacum/sassafras/colocynth decoction, and sweating.

Continuation of medical recipes for swellings, tumors, and foot/knee complaints, including decoctions of guaiacum and sassafras, lye washes with rock salt and quicksilver, a cerate for the knee, and cataplasms using cow/pigeon dung and mercurial water.

Conclusion of recipes for swellings (liniments and cataplasms), followed by an illustrated section 'Von Schwinden der Glider' (On the Wasting/Atrophy of the Limbs) with a colored drawing of a gesturing man, and recipes for baths, mixtures, and ointments for wasting limbs.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Anfang. / Von Schwinden der Glider** (`#xywh=400,400,2138,1000`): Colored pen-and-ink illustration in the lower-left column showing a half-length figure of a bearded man with shoulder-length brown hair, wearing a pinkish-red doublet with green-and-gold frogging/braiding and a white collar, standing behind a rectangular parapet or ledge. His right hand rests on his chest while his left arm is extended to the right, gesturing toward the opposite column. Below the ledge on the left is a small rectangular cartouche inscribed 'Anfang.' ('Beginning.'), with folio number '246' written in the left margin above the ledge.

Further ointments and a plaster for wasting limbs, a theoretical explanation of post-wound limb atrophy (loss of nourishing humor and corruption of the three principles), and an alchemical preparation of feather alum with rectified mercury followed by an ointment and plaster.

Medical/surgical treatise on rose-fistulas and ulcers (Von denen Rosen fistlen Vnd Geschweren), their causes, diagnostic signs (including bone caries and joint involvement), palliative vs. curative treatment, and recipes for plasters, injections, and washes. Top-left features a portrait of a young woman.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**aufgehört.** (`#xywh=400,400,2130,1000`): Half-length watercolor-tinted ink portrait of a young woman facing forward/slightly left, with brown hair in a braided updo, wearing a red coral necklace, a laced red-and-grey/blue bodice over a white puffed-sleeve chemise, and raising her left hand with a red, black-spotted cuff. She stands behind a horizontal fluted parapet/ledge inscribed 'aufgehört.' in brown ink.

Continuation of fistula and ulcer treatments, featuring recipes for medicated waters, ointments (including Unguentum Basilicum and the 'factotum Magistri'), plasters for skull ulcers near the periosteum, and instructions for preparing a pressed wax-and-resin bath-sponge tent (illustrated in the right column) to dilate narrow fistulas and treat callosities.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**** (`#xywh=400,400,2323,1000`): Hand-drawn, yellow-tinted watercolor illustration of a porous, two-lobed bath sponge (Badeschwamm) with dark ink stippling representing pores, positioned in the upper-middle right column beside the recipe for preparing a medicated sponge tent.

Section on carious bones (Cariosi Baines), detailing surgical access, scraping/searing, and powders/infusions (including euphorbium, birthwort, guaiacum, iris, and calcined chalk) to treat rotten bones and draw out splinters; followed by a new rubricated section on oil-fillers/balsams (Von Etlichen Oel Füllner), beginning with 'the Black Lion' (der Schwarze Leb). Includes illustrations of a bare foot resting on a block and a standing yellow lion.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**** (`#xywh=400,400,2172,1000`): Upper left: Watercolor-tinted ink illustration of a bare human lower leg and foot resting on a rectangular wooden block/stone on a grassy ground, accompanying the section on carious bones (Cariosi Baines).

**** (`#xywh=400,400,2172,1000`): Lower left: Watercolor-tinted ink illustration of a standing golden-yellow lion facing left with a flowing mane and curled tail on brownish-green ground, accompanying the recipe 'Ein füllner der Schwarze Leb genandt' ('A filler/balsam called the Black Lion').

Page 557 (verso) contains corrosive and caustic powder and ointment recipes for fistulas, eye fistulas, and foul wounds, including a rubricated recipe titled 'Der Graue Wolff' (The Grey Wolf) illustrated with a painted wolf, as well as several further corrosive ointments ('Egents Sälbl', 'Egentte Salbn', 'Ezung ohne Schmerzen').

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Ein anders der Graue Wolff genandt.** (`#xywh=400,400,2314,1000`): Colour-washed pen-and-ink illustration of a grey-brown wolf standing in profile facing left on a patch of ochre-green ground, positioned in the upper-left column beside the recipe ingredients for 'Der Graue Wolff'.

**tz Puluär Gar kröfftig** (`#xywh=400,400,2314,1000`): Small painted reddish-brown oval diagram (representing a medicinal pellet or troche) placed inline between the two halves of the rubricated heading 'tz Puluär' and 'Gar kröfftig' in the right column.

Page 559 (verso) concludes the flesh-growing powder from p. 558, gives instructions for testing precipitated mercury on a coal, and introduces a new surgical section titled 'Von Angeloffnen Schbarzen painern' (On swollen black/necrotic bones) illustrated with a seated figure pointing to a cautery/scraping instrument near the leg.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Von Angeloffnen Schbarzen painern** (`#xywh=400,400,2319,1000`): Colour-washed pen-and-ink illustration in the middle of the left column showing the lower body and legs of a seated figure wearing a yellow doublet, pinkish-red breeches, and a black shoe, extending their right leg forward and pointing with the left hand toward a small metal surgical instrument (cautery iron or bone scraper) resting on the ground near the ankle.

Surgical and pharmaceutical recipes for fluxes, corrupted flesh, and wound-healing powders (including preparations with mercury, litharge, camphor, terra sigillata, Armenian bole, tutia, and burnt lead), followed by a colored illustration of a pointing hand and a section in red ink on treating a whitlow/felon ('Von dem Wurm an finger') and preparing precipitated mercury ('precipitat pp.').

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Pointing hand (top of right column)** (`#xywh=400,400,2133,1000`): Colored ink and wash illustration at the top of the right column depicting a right hand with the index finger extended horizontally to the right, resting above a double horizontal blue/teal ink rule.

Continuation of the preparation of dulcified mercury precipitate ('☿ precipitat. dulcinicirt'), followed by a colored illustration of a man firing a musket and a rubricated section on gunshot wounds ('Von den Geschoßnen Wunden'), including oleum catellorum (oil of puppies), salves, and powders for extracting gunpowder and shot from wounds.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Man firing a musket (Von den Geschoßnen Wunden)** (`#xywh=400,400,2328,1000`): Colored ink and wash illustration in the middle of the left column depicting a bearded man in profile facing left, wearing a wide-brimmed dark hat with a feather and a green-and-ochre doublet, aiming and firing a long musket/arquebus to the left with a puff of grey smoke and red-orange flame rising from the firing pan, above a horizontal tan ledge.

Early New High German medical and apothecary recipes (verso, p. 503) in two columns. The left column continues treatments for burns and gangrene (using frog spawn, green willow bark in butter, egg white with prepared tutty, rose oil, linseed oil, unslaked lime, and litharge). The right column contains three rubricated recipes in red ink for frostbitten hands and feet in winter, swelling of the feet, and a precious medicinal water (with mercury sublimate) for rising, swelling, ulcers, and scabby eruptions of the feet and hands.

Surgical treatise 'Von fistlen in Gemain' (Of fistulas in general), accompanied by a watercolor illustration of a seated man with red lesions/fistulas on his face, arms, and legs. The text discusses probing fistulas to assess depth and hidden passages, widening openings with tent dilators (Stellmeißel), deciding between surgical excision/cauterization and palliative care near major nerves and blood vessels, and supporting local treatment with strict diet, purgatives, decoctions, and wound potions.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**[Untitled illustration of a man afflicted with fistulas/lesions]** (`#xywh=400,400,2159,1000`): Rectangular watercolor illustration framed in red ink in the upper half of the left column. It depicts a man with shoulder-length brown hair wearing a pinkish-tan tunic with green collar, cuffs, and a green sash, seated or crouching on green-and-ochre grassy ground with low green bushes to the left. His left arm is extended to the right and his bare legs are stretched forward; his face, arms, hands, and legs are covered with numerous small red spots representing fistulas or ulcers. Faint, faded markings appear near the upper border of the illustration.

Early New High German medical/apothecary manuscript (Wellcome MS.990, p. 565, verso). The left column concludes a treatment note and presents a rubricated section on the signs and diagnosis of fistulas (distinguishing marrow, nerve/membrane, flesh, blood-vessel, and carious-bone fistulas, followed by dietary and caustic treatment advice). The right column begins a rubricated section on fistulas of the breast/chest, followed by four Latin-German apothecary recipes: a precious plaster for fistulas with preparation instructions, two salves/liniments, and a caustic wash for spongy flesh in fistulas.

Recto folio 566 (pencil foliation 253) containing the conclusion of a fistula treatment, two recipes for wound drinks for fistulas ('Wundt Trankh in den fistlen' and 'Ein anders Trankh in den fistlen'), general surgical advice on purging, diet, bandaging, cutting, and cauterizing stubborn fistulas, and a large watercolor illustration of seven surgical instruments (two curved fistula knives, two straight bistouries/probes, surgical scissors, and three cautery irons).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**diser Vnder glich Instrumenta ~** (`#xywh=400,400,2161,1000`): Large watercolor illustration occupying the lower half of the page, depicting seven surgical instruments for treating fistulas: two curved sickle-shaped bistouries/syringotomes with slender probe tips at the top; a straight probe/director with a turned dark wooden handle; a straight probe-pointed bistoury with a light brown wooden handle; a pair of surgical shears/scissors with looped spring-like handles; and three long-shafted actual cautery irons with turned wooden handles and variously shaped tips (triangular/hatchet, bulbous/olivary, and flat disc).

Recto folio 568 (pencil foliation 254) in two-column layout, featuring a watercolor illustration of a patient reclining in bed covered with red fistula sores/pustules, followed by 'Von den fistlen des Vndern Leibs' (On fistulas of the lower body), a cataplasm recipe, and several fistula/wound-water recipes ('Ein khöstliches Waser in den fistlen', 'Ein anders', 'Waser zuo den fistlen darmit zuo Rainigen ohne Schmerzen', 'Khöstliches Wundt Waser').

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Patient suffering from fistulas/sores (above 'Von den fistlen des Vndern Leibs')** (`#xywh=400,400,2133,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the upper left column showing a figure with brown curly hair lying half-reclining on a wooden bed with white sheets and pillow, uncovered to the thighs, with numerous red spots/ulcers/fistulas across the chest, abdomen, arms, and legs. Beyond the bed to the right is a green-and-ochre landscape with trees.

A two-column recto page (p. 569) containing a rubricated recipe for 'Ein Wunderbahrliches Waser' (A Miraculous Water) that cures fistulas by distilling turpentine, frankincense, aloe, mastic, galangal, saffron, cubebs, ivy gum, nutmeg, cinnamon, and cloves into three fractions (aqua balsami, oleum balsamum, balsamo artificialiter), followed by instructions on treating fistulas on the head, neck, and in Neapolitan disease (syphilis) with purgatives, wound drinks, and caustic/mercury-based applications.

  <em>Facsimile: Canvas #515 (verso, Page 570) · <a href="https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0515.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg" target="_blank">View Full-Resolution IIIF</a></em>

A two-column verso page (p. 570, pencil foliation 255) continuing fistula treatments with digestive salves, turpentine-balsam, and a watercolor/ink-wash illustration of a surgical probe/spatula, followed by recipes for wax/precipitate cones ('schöll weigel'). A rubricated section 'Von den Glid. Waser.' (On Synovial Fluid / Joint-Water) begins at the bottom of the left column and continues on the right column with pain-stilling salves and cataplasms.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Surgical probe or spatula** (`#xywh=400,400,2141,1000`): Horizontal ink-wash and pale ochre watercolor drawing in the middle of the left column depicting an elongated, flat surgical instrument (probe/spatula) with a rounded blunt tip on the left and a flared, trefoil-shaped handle on the right.

A two-column recto page (p. 571) continuing the treatment of joint-water ('glid waser') with plasters (Emplastrum Basiliconis, diasulphuris, diapalma, diachylon), a cataplasm to strengthen the limb and disperse swelling, a wound powder for internal and external wounds and nerve injuries, and several short recipes ('Ein anders fürs glid waser', 'Ein Anders') using pigeon dung, egg white, saffron, alum, and burnt leather.

Full-height watercolor of a wounded man ('Wundmann') in the left column showing weapons, lesions, ulcers, a dog, and a snake/cord at his ankle; right column begins the section on wounds and dangerous injuries, specifically hot and cold gangrene (Gangraena and Sphacelus).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Wundmann (Wound Man) illustration** (`#xywh=400,400,2171,1000`): Full-height watercolor in the left column depicting a standing nude man wearing a yellow-ochre loincloth in a grassy landscape with distant trees and faint blue-grey clouds above. His body exhibits multiple wounds, red pustules, ulcers, and weapons: a curved sabre/scimitar piercing the crown of his head, a yellow club/cudgel striking the left side of his head, a red swelling on the right neck, a dagger in his left chest, a large red ulcer on his left upper arm, a blade through his left forearm, a sword piercing his left thigh, red/purple sores on his knees and shins, a grey dog sitting on the grass to the right, and a snake or cord coiled around his right ankle.

Continuation of the treatise on hot and cold gangrene (Gangraena and Sphacelus), distinguishing their clinical signs, the role of the vital spirits (Spiritus Vitales) and radical moisture (humidum radicale), and the four humoral causes (blood, bile, phlegm, melancholy).

Continuation of a treatise on inflammation and swelling, followed by a rubricated section on the cure and healing of hot gangrene ('heisen Brandts') arising from superfluous moisture, heat, or dryness, including dietary/surgical advice and recipes for defensive ointments, bloodletting/purging boluses, washes, and cataplasms.

Continuation of gangrene remedies, followed by a rubricated section on causes from heat and dryness in erysipelas ('Rotlauff oder Schön'), and a rubricated section on arresting frostbite ('Erfrohren Auffhalten') with recipes for washes, salves, and cataplasms.

Continuation of frostbite cataplasm, followed by a rubricated section on gangrene caused by excessive dryness ('Ursachen auß Zů großen Drückne'), detailing dietary regimen, moistening baths, salves, plasters, surgical debridement, and a celery-juice salve ('Sälbel auß Eppich').

Page 578 (fol. 259r) contains recipes for earthworm oil (Regenwürmöll), a treatise on the poisonous properties of gangrene/inflammation with sweating draughts using theriac, mithridate, bezoar, dittany, and angelica, and instructions for scarification, leeches, and a warm decoction.

Surgical instructions and recipes for treating gangrene (der heiße und kalte Brand), including wound debridement of the eschar, application of Unguentum Aegyptiacum and cataplasms, internal theriac/mithridate with blessed thistle water, cauterization or excision, and a rubricated red-ink salve and cataplasms for hot and cold gangrene.

Treatise section 'Von dem Krebs' (Of Cancer), accompanied by a watercolor illustration of a reclining woman with a red crab clinging to her left breast (numbered 435.). Describes the onset, progression, pain, and malignancy of breast cancer, followed by internal antidotes and blood-cleansing remedies (diaphoretic powders, Bezoardicum Joviale et Martiale, Sal Saturni, viper powders, herbal distillates, and volatile spirits).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**435.** (`#xywh=400,400,2335,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the upper-left column showing a female patient reclining on a blue-and-white striped pillow, wearing a red cap and a grey garment open at the chest, with a bright red crab/lobster clinging to her left breast to symbolize breast cancer ('Krebs'). Framed below by a gold-and-brown band bearing the number '435.'.

Page 585 (verso) contains a recipe for a cleansing and healing salve for cancerous pain (using nightshade juice, crab juice, litharge, ceruse, rose water, myrtle oil, lily oil, tutty, precipitated mercury, and calamine), followed by a rubricated section on general and easier remedies for cancer, discussing the difficulty of curing cancer, the role of melancholic humor, and the three names of cancer (Noli me tangere, Lupus, and Krebs).

### Left Column

| Line | German Diplomatic (Original) | English Translation & Editorial Notes |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |

Page 588 (recto, pencil foliation 264) begins with a faded rubricated heading, a styptic powder recipe (tragacanth, gum arabic, comfrey root, carpenter's glue), and then presents a rubricated account of an Italian ('Welscher') surgeon known as the 'Krebs Doctor' who cured cancers across Germany using a caustic arsenic-soot-arum powder, followed by protective defensive plasters and soothing ointments (frankincense, mummy, mastic, myrrh, aloes, sarcocolla, opopanax, litharge).

Page 587 (verso) features a striking watercolor illustration of a woman undergoing surgical excision of a breast cancer (with a knife and crossed needles/ligatures), followed by a rubricated surgical procedure ('Wie der Krebs an der Brust Soll geschnitten werden') detailing how to tie four threads through the breast, pull it forward, excise the tumor, cauterize bleeding vessels with a hot iron, and dress the wound. The right column concludes a preceding note and displays a rubricated heading and full-length watercolor illustrations of surgical instruments (cautery irons, a large excision knife, and surgical needles/probes).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Surgical excision of breast cancer** (`#xywh=400,400,2321,1000`): Watercolor and ink bust illustration of a bare-chested woman wearing a blue-grey headscarf/coif, showing a large ulcerated breast tumor transfixed by a horizontal surgical knife and two crossed needles/pins with red ligature threads hanging downward, set above an olive-green painted border.

**Instrumenta Welche Zu dieser operation gebraucht werden.** (`#xywh=400,400,2321,1000`): Full-column watercolor and ink illustration of surgical instruments used for breast cancer excision: two long-handled cautery irons with turned brown wooden handles (one with a rectangular flat plate head and one with a round disc head), a large broad-bladed surgical knife with a carved wooden handle, and two slender surgical needles/probes on the far right.

Page 590 (recto, pencil foliation 265) continues a caustic/remedy for cancer with honey and litharge, followed by a framed watercolor illustration of a dog biting a man's ankle, and recipes/medical discourse on rabid dog bites ('Winige Hundts Biss'), venomous animal bites (wasps, bees, snakes, scorpions), and internal/external antidotes.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Anfang.** (`#xywh=400,400,2137,1000`): Framed watercolor illustration (blue and black ink border) depicting the lower body and bare legs of a person wearing reddish-brown breeches and holding a staff in the left hand, while a small brown dog bites the back of their left ankle, drawing bright red blood. Inscribed 'Anfang.' at the bottom right.

Page 589 (verso) contains a series of surgical and alchemical recipes for treating cancer ('Krebs') and fistulas ('Fistel'), including 'Himmel farbes Wasser in Den Krebs' (sky-colored water for cancer), 'Ein beraites Unguentum Vor den krebs', 'Ein anders Köstliches mittel', 'Für Krebs und Fistel', 'Volgentes Salbel thuet Wunder wirckhen im Krebs' (using green frogs filled with butter), and 'Volgentes Pulver hat Welt herren Curiert'.

Page 592 (recto, pencil foliation 266) concludes the discussion of rabid animal bites (dogs, cats, snakes, scorpions) and blistering plasters/cupping treatments, followed by recipes for 'Der Hunde. Rosse. vnd Stieren biß' and 'Wan dich ein adter gebissen' (adder bite), a framed watercolor illustration of a person afflicted with pustules/scabies, and the opening of a chapter 'Von den Krezen' (On Scabies).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Von den Krezen** (`#xywh=400,400,2152,1000`): Framed watercolor illustration (blue and black ink border) showing a half-length profile of a fair-haired person in a reddish-brown tunic behind a horizontal bar, raising their right arm; their face, neck, and arms are covered in dark reddish-brown spots and pustules illustrating scabies ('Krezen').

Page 593 (recto) of Wellcome MS.990 contains purgative recipes, decoctions, and bath and ointment remedies for scabies/itching (Krozen), including a watercolor illustration of a sulfur-soaked shirt worn for 5-6 days to cure itching.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Medicated Shirt for Curing Itching (Scabies)** (`#xywh=400,400,2315,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the right column depicting a knee-length, blue-and-white vertically striped shirt or tunic with short sleeves, standing on a small patch of green ground. The surrounding text explains soaking a shirt in sulfur water, drying it, and wearing it on the bare body for 5 to 6 days to cure itching without ointments.

Page 595 (recto) opens a new section on smallpox/pustules ('Von den Fladern der Kinder und alten Leüten'), featuring a watercolor portrait of a person with facial pustules, followed by etiology, prognosis, bloodletting/laxative advice, and internal remedies (antimony, bezoar, hartshorn, pulvis ruber pannonicus).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Person Afflicted with Facial Pustules (Smallpox / Fladern)** (`#xywh=400,400,2358,1000`): Watercolor illustration at the top of the left column depicting the head and shoulders of a person wearing a blue cap or headscarf and a pinkish-red pleated garment, with reddish-brown spots and pustules covering the face, framed at the bottom by a horizontal bar above the rubricated heading.

Continuation of smallpox (Fladen) remedies: internal diaphoretics (carduus benedictus syrup, fumitory/scabious waters, Alkermes lozenges), remedies for suppressed eruption (hartshorn, bezoar/castoreum in broth), cooling gargles for smallpox in the mouth and throat, clearing blocked nostrils with butter and Marian water, and eye washes/ointments for swollen eyelids and eyes.

Continuation of smallpox (Fladen) care: protecting the eyes, prognostic signs, preventing facial pitting with barley mucilage, bean meal, egg oil, and virgin's milk, and removing pustules. Followed by a new section on 'Mania. Unsinnigkeit Verliehrung des Verstandts' (madness/loss of reason), describing its causes, symptoms, emetics, bloodletting, and diet.

Continuation of Mania (purging, bloodletting, and a rubricated 'Secretum' using dog brain). Followed by a new section on 'Ascheren Und Bluett Aissen' (carbuncles and blood-boils / furuncles), classifying parotids, axillary buboes, carbuncles, and pestilential swellings, and a subsection on 'Achslen Geschwern' (axillary abscesses).

Medical and surgical recipes for treating abscesses, gangrene, and wounds, including cataplasms, digestive salves, plasters (diasulphuris, diapalma, diachylon simplex), and internal wound potions.

Recipes for blood-purifying essences and plasters for poisonous/plague abscesses, accompanied by a watercolor illustration of a seated figure with an extended bare leg, and a chapter on ulcers and abscesses (Ulcus, Abscessus).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Seated figure with extended bare leg** (`#xywh=400,400,2102,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the upper right column showing a seated figure from the waist down, wearing a green-sleeved garment and draped pink/reddish cloth, extending a bare right leg and foot resting on a yellowish-brown mound above a green-and-brown base, with the left hand pointing right.

Watercolor illustration of a bent lower leg and foot, followed by a treatise on Spina Ventosa ('Bain Krebs / Bain fresser / Bain falle'), describing its origins in young boys and girls, progression through bone and periosteum, fistulous ulcers, corrosive blood, and initial purgative treatment.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Bain Krebs. Bain fresser / Bain falle.** (`#xywh=400,400,2080,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the upper left column showing a seated figure's lower body from the hip down, clad in a green tunic and dark grey-brown draped breeches, with a bare, bent lower leg and foot resting on a narrow strip of green and yellow ground.

Medical and surgical recipes including preparations for vapor/fume ('Anders duft'), corrosive sublimate ointment for open salted fluxes and ringworm, coral salt for liver flux, remedies for urinary retention, decrepitation of sea salt, drawing plaster, softening a hardened spleen, loss of appetite, plaster for poisoned blisters, and preventing smallpox pockmarks in children.

Treatise on recognizing and treating poisoning ('Wan ainen Giff Vergeben Worden'): symptoms of hot/sharp poisons (arsenic, sublimate, orpiment, antimony) versus cold poisons (opium, cicuta, nightshade, henbane, mandrake), antidotes (olive/almond oil, mithridate, scordium, bezoar in blessed thistle water), and dry/moist poisons.

Continuation of remedies for poisoning (vomiting, clysters, purging, sneezing) and treatments for venomous animal bites (cupping, scarification, baths, scorpion oil, terra sigillata, theriac, laudanum). Followed by alchemical preparations of antimony oil and mercury (making mercury non-corrosive and preparing it for internal medicinal use against leprosy and syphilis), and the beginning of a section on the uses and effects of mercury.

Continuation of the preparation and therapeutic uses of mercury (for sores, plague pustules, melancholy, quartan fever, colic, worms, pleurisy, podagra), followed by recipes for mercury precipitate, a painless corrosive for setting fontanels, a gentle laxative electuary, and cupping/scarification treatment for sciatica with a watercolor diagram.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Sciatica cupping diagram** (`#xywh=400,400,2336,1000`): Small circular watercolor drawing in blue-grey and brown washes in the lower right column showing the placement of cupping glasses and scarification marks on the hip for sciatica.

Conclusion of the sciatica treatment (purging with Species Hermodactili Compositae), followed by a section on lung abscess / phthisis (goat's milk with rose sugar, china root, almond oil, comfrey electuary, silver/tin tincture), and a section on throat abscesses, swelling, and inflammation (clysters, bloodletting, diaphoretic drink, gargle water, and external plaster of album graecum and swallows' nests when suppurating).

Upper half features a watercolor illustration of a patient in bed and in a sweating/fumigation box for the salivation cure. Lower half introduces the cure of salivation (Chur der salifacian), listing indicated diseases (syphilis, leprosy, paralysis, chronic ulcers) in red ink, contraindications (consumptives), and cautions regarding patient strength.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Illustration of the salivation and sweating cure** (`#xywh=400,400,200,1000`): Rectangular watercolor and ink drawing across the top half of the page. On the left, a patient lies in a wooden bed under a green-and-white patterned blanket next to a small green-topped table with two vessels. In the center is a closed yellow wooden door with black iron hinges and latch. On the right stands a yellow wooden sweating box (Schwitzkasten) with a small hinged front door and the patient's head protruding from the slanted top.

Post-salivation care including sweating, diet, and a strengthening herbal drink; notes on driving salivation with Turpeth Mineral, mercury precipitate, and Arcanum Corallinum; followed by a new rubricated section 'Von der Neapolischen kranckheit, das Seindt Franosen' (On the Neapolitan Disease / Syphilis), dividing the disease into three stages and listing diagnostic signs.

Continuation of a medical treatise on syphilis (Franzosenkrankheit / Morbus Gallicus), detailing its symptoms (pustules, bone pains, ulceration of the uvula, tonsils, throat, and genitals, dark circles under the eyes, general weakness, and latency periods) and five methods of treatment: (1) the wood cure (guaiac, sassafras, sarsaparilla, China root), (2) purgation with mercurials (mercurius dulcis, arcanum corallinum, white precipitate, turpethum minerale), (3) the fumigation/smoke cure with cinnabar, (4) the inunction/ointment cure with mercury, and (5) bathing in mercurial sublimate water. The author concludes that among these five cures, the mercury inunction cure is the best and most reliable.

Continuation of instructions for mercury inunction (salivation) therapy for venereal disease, detailing the frequency and anatomical sites of ointment application, sweating in bed, linen changes, monitoring for gum swelling and salivation onset, avoiding excessive mercury or cold, and post-salivation restorative care.

Features a watercolor illustration of a medicated bath cure, followed by a rubricated chapter 'Von der Bad Chur in diser wilen Vnd schändlichen kranckhheit' describing a mercury-sublimate bath cure in a covered wooden tub with a hole for the head, preceded by purging with Arcana Corollini, bloodletting, and Mercurius dulcis.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Medicated Bath Cure (Bad Chur)** (`#xywh=400,400,200,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the left column above the rubricated heading, showing a patient submerged up to the neck in a round wooden tub (Wanne) filled with grey-blue water, while an attendant in a red blouse and green skirt enters from a doorway on the left holding a red goblet.

Treatises on syphilitic ulcers in various parts of the body, beginning with ulcers in the urethra, followed by rubricated sections on ulcers in general, buboes (Aider Bülen) with cataplasms and Emplastrum diachylum, syphilitic tophi treated with Emplastrum de ranis cum mercurio, and cleansing ripe ulcers.

Continuation of wound and ulcer treatments: compound balsams, ointments, and plasters (Vnguentum Supuratiuum, Balsam Italicum, Emplastrum diasulphuris), followed by a rubricated section and watercolor illustration for 'Wolff oder fresente geschwer' (wolf or devouring ulcer).

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Wolff oder fresente geschwer** (`#xywh=400,400,200,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the lower right column depicting a grey wolf standing on a patch of green grass, facing left, illustrating the 'wolf or devouring ulcer' (Wolff oder fresente geschwer).

Opening of the pediatric section ('Von Khranckheiten dere Khinder') featuring a large domestic nursery watercolor illustration, an overview of childhood illnesses, and a section on macrocephaly ('Erstlich Von den Groskhopffeten Khindern') with humoral theory and remedies.

### Illustrations and Anatomical Diagrams

**Krankheiten der Kinder — Domestic nursery scene** (`#xywh=400,400,200,1000`): Watercolor illustration in the upper left column showing an interior room with a leaded window, a green-topped table and chair, a swaddled infant lying in a wooden rocking cradle, a small boy wearing a feathered cap and carrying a hobby horse/stick, and a woman standing in a doorway gesturing toward the child.
